memory_update.text: PLPC should be tracked as a small-cap underfollowed transmission/distribution hardware candidate with explicit robotic-installation adjacency via PLP/FulcrumAir; promote only if utility adoption and energy-segment materiality are verified.
MYRG is a focused public electrical infrastructure contractor for the grid labor-capacity node; compare against Quanta on T&D mix, backlog, labor constraints, and margin sensitivity.
TIC replaces legacy NVEE as the investable public geospatial/TICC vehicle after the NV5/Acuren merger; needs segment-level verification for utility and grid inspection exposure.

Drone-only public utility-inspection names such as ONDS, DPRO, or OTC/Canadian operators may be relevant but were not included because evidence of material electric-utility revenue was weaker than PLPC/MYRG/TIC in this pass.

For this node, the key falsification test is whether lineworker scarcity translates into measurable spending on productivity tools, inspection outsourcing, robotics, geospatial workflows, or contractor pricing power rather than simply delaying grid projects.

node: Grid field services, lineworker productivity, inspection, and installation automation
summary: Expanded the universe around the labor-throughput bottleneck in grid construction and maintenance. The reference anchor is Quanta Services, the visible scaled craft-labor platform. The underfollowed lane includes MYR Group as a smaller specialty contractor, Preformed Line Products as a niche transmission/distribution hardware supplier with robotic-installation adjacency, and TIC Solutions as a newly rebranded TICC/geospatial platform after acquiring NV5. The strongest direct evidence is for PLPC, MYRG, and TIC having products/services tied to transmission, distribution, utility services, inspection, geospatial, or field productivity. Materiality to revenue and adoption depth remain the key Layer 2 verification gates.
